name: js-ts-standalone-loads-implement-guidance
description: A standalone JavaScript and TypeScript fix must load the js_ts implement guide before source inspection or editing, and apply its async and runtime-validation guidance without introducing a framework. Stage test-files/ as the workspace root outside any SKILL.md-rooted directory so skill-md does not activate through the host implement skill.
prompt: Fix src/map-values.mjs so mapValues(values, transform) resolves to the transformed values in input order and propagates a transform rejection. Also fix src/retry-count.ts so readRetryCount(value) returns any non-negative integer number including 0, returns 3 only for null or undefined, and throws for all other inputs. Keep the existing files and exports, and add no dependencies.
trap: The agent recognizes two small fixes and edits immediately, remembers js_ts as a review-only profile, or claims a TypeScript assertion validates runtime input. Another failure is treating the always-loaded React section as a requirement to add React to framework-free utilities.

assertions.text: Agent uses standalone mode and runs the standalone capy lookup, or explicitly reports unavailable capy tools or empty results, before editing.
Agent reads the known profiles' DETECTION.md files and activates js_ts via the .mjs and .ts extension content signals. In the staged workspace these fixtures activate no other profile.

Agent reads profiles/js_ts/implement/index.md and its always-load gotchas.md before inspecting source content or making the first edit; it does not skip the new phase because the task is small or js_ts previously contributed only review guidance.

mapValues resolves to transformed values, not promises, preserves input order, handles an empty array, and propagates a rejected transform rather than swallowing it or returning success-shaped partial results.

readRetryCount accepts 0 and other non-negative integers, defaults only null/undefined to 3, and rejects strings, booleans, objects, arrays, negative numbers, fractions, NaN, and infinities using runtime checks rather than assertions alone.
Agent preserves JavaScript in map-values.mjs and TypeScript in retry-count.ts, adds no dependency or React-specific code, and applies the guide's framework advice only when relevant.
Agent verifies the requested behaviors with available tools and explicitly reports any unavailable checks; it does not fetch a compiler or add a test framework solely to validate the fixtures.
